solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plan that's misplaced at religious building

indicators.note: something misplaced has gone missing, so the word at is lost from the plan

parts.note: a template is a pattern or plan to work from
taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect's plan was mislaid at the site of a church being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's misplaced' removes AT from TEMPLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building dedicated to worship, as in a Hindu or Jewish place of prayer.

clue.text: Soviet city left covered in blight: Government gets radical

indicators.note: the letter for left is enclosed by the word for blight

parts.note: a stain is a blemish or blight

explanation.surface: A political report: a Soviet city in decline, its government turning radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts L inside STAIN to give STALIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad, now Volgograd, was a major city of the USSR, famous for the WWII siege.

clue.text: Sailor and ship beset by busy people (religious types)

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common crossword sailor

indicators.note: the ship's letters are surrounded by the busy people

parts.note: busy as a bee, so bees are busy people
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor and his ship are surrounded by bustling people, here nuns perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy people' are bees, from 'busy as a bee'; the brackets warn that the definition is the religious types, not the busy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbesses are the women heading convents of nuns, so they are religious figures.

clue.text: University line supporting English location of 2, 5, 6, 7, 17A, 17D, 23, 29 and 30

indicators.note: in a down clue the university and line sit beneath English, holding it up

parts.note: a rope is a line, especially at sea

explanation.surface: Reads as a cross-reference puzzle about a university course backing English.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-referenced answers are all European cities, towns, rivers or mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent where Stalingrad, Rome, Paris, the Pyrenees and the Danube all lie.

clue.text: Bus trips taking precedence over railway after damp start to day in town

indicators.note: the shuffled bus letters come after the dew
the jumbled bus goes in front of the railway letters

parts.note: dew is the moisture found early in the morning

indicators.note: a bus that trips stumbles, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Buses get priority over trains on a wet morning in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' turns BUS into SBU.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewsbury is a town in West Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Indifferent painting capturing North European river

indicators.note: the daub holds the letter for North inside it

parts.note: a daub is a crude, poor painting

explanation.surface: A mediocre painting depicts a river in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts N inside DAUB to give DANUB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube flows across central Europe from Germany to the Black Sea.

clue.text: City church abandoning shiny fittings

indicators.note: the church letters are given up, leaving the rest of the fittings

parts.note: chrome is the bright metal plating on fittings

explanation.surface: A city church strips out its gleaming fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes CH from CHROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital of Italy, the Eternal City.

clue.text: Die after lethal shot in hip?

indicators.note: the word for die follows the jumble
something shot is wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to die, as in 'when I go'

explanation.surface: Someone dies after a fatal bullet wound to the hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' turns LETHAL into ALLTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old idiom for very fashionable, the height of style, just as hip means trendy.

clue.text: Recalled Hill routine ending in joke Shakespeare quotation

indicators.note: called back, so the hill word runs backwards

parts.note: a butte is a steep isolated hill
a rut is a dull routine

indicators.note: only the final letter of joke is used

explanation.surface: A comedian's old routine ends with a joke built on a Shakespeare line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns BUTTE into ETTUB. Benny Hill was a British TV comic, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's dying words to his friend in Julius Caesar, 'And you, Brutus?'

clue.text: Twelve letters left for island

parts.note: the first twelve letters of the alphabet run A to L

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a dozen letters behind on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve letters' is read as A TO L, the span of the alphabet's first twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: What'll quicken if you're full of beans?

definitions.text: What'll quicken if you're full of beans?

parts.words: What'll quicken if you're full of beans?
parts.note: a lively person's heartbeat races; and beans themselves are legumes, the dried seed type

explanation.surface: A question about what speeds up when you are bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of beans' means energetic, so the heartbeat quickens; it also hints at legumes, the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The heartbeat felt at the wrist rises with excitement; dried beans and lentils share the same name.

clue.text: Least familiar science graduate found in part of Oxbridge with others

indicators.note: the graduate's letters sit inside the university's

parts.note: OU is Oxford University, one half of Oxbridge
a BSc is a Bachelor of Science
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: An obscure science graduate turns up at Oxford or Cambridge among others.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxbridge is the joint name for Oxford and Cambridge universities, so Oxford University is one part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of obscure: the least known or most unfamiliar.

clue.text: Schooner, perhaps, not offering hot drink

indicators.note: the hot letter is withheld from the vessel

parts.note: a schooner is one kind of sailing vessel
H is short for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A schooner glass of sherry that isn't a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not offering' takes H from SHIP. A schooner is also a large sherry glass, the surface's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sip is a small mouthful taken when drinking, and the verb means to drink slowly.

clue.text: Birds navy's kept in view when returning

indicators.note: the navy letters are held inside
the word for view goes backwards

parts.note: to view is to see
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors keep birds in sight on the voyage home.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word for view is turned round; the navy's letters go into it forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, a crossword staple among birds of prey.

clue.text: Count, Earl and Knight are mute after a shock

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: shaken up, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A count, an earl and a knight are left speechless by a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a shock' turns ARE MUTE into UMERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to tally items one by one, a verb sense of the clue's nobleman.

clue.text: A small amount around that place's finally, finally prepared

indicators.note: the small amount wraps the place word

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
there means that place

indicators.note: the first finally signals taking the last letter of the second

explanation.surface: A little hesitation, then, finally, everything there is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts THERE inside A TAD; the first 'finally' picks Y, the last letter of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready for immediate use or action, like a weapon held up and prepared.

clue.text: Millions invested in repairs to broken transport system

indicators.note: the million letter is placed within
a broken thing must be put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written
M is short for million

explanation.surface: Millions spent on fixing a failing transport network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges REPAIRS TO and 'invested in' sets M among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital's underground railway network, a city transport system.

clue.text: Blaze observed to rise in mountains

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of burning wood

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards

parts.note: seen means observed

explanation.surface: A blaze is spotted climbing up a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns SEEN into NEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain range forming the border between France and Spain.

clue.text: Friend not on call

indicators.note: the word on is left out of the friend

parts.note: a crony is a close pal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend isn't available to take a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ON from CRONY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry is a shout or call, as of a street vendor or bird.

clue.text: Lady making introductions bringing in start of carriage trade

indicators.note: the host takes a letter inside

parts.note: a commère is a female compère, a woman host introducing acts

indicators.note: only the opening letter of carriage

explanation.surface: A hostess ushers in the first carriage at a trade show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' puts C inside COMMERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is the buying and selling of goods, business dealings on a large scale.

clue.text: See 17
The writer's permitted to discount article with more tolerant views?

parts.note: the setter's writer refers to himself as me

indicators.note: to leave out the article from the word for permitted

parts.note: allowed means permitted
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer is allowed to ignore a piece that shows a softer outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to discount' removes A from ALLOWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has mellowed has softened with age, becoming gentler and less rigid in opinion.

clue.text: Fish: lands more at sea

indicators.note: confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fishing boat brings in a bigger catch out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges LANDS MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sockeye, a Pacific species with deep red flesh.

clue.text: A new solution of maths problem concerning pipes?

indicators.note: the maths letters are freshly worked out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh answer to a mathematics problem about plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new solution of' turns MATHS into STHMA; 'pipes' are the airways, not plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a condition that narrows the airways of the lungs, the body's breathing tubes.

clue.text: Standard computer network upset about damaged ROM

indicators.note: the turned network surrounds the rest
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: LAN is a local area network

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A standard network crashes because of corrupted read-only memory.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' reads the network letters from the bottom up; 'about' sets the jumbled memory letters inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual or conforming to the standard.

clue.text: Subject provided as example in story

indicators.note: the example letters sit inside the story

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A subject for a story is supplied as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: Liège is also a Belgian city, one of the European places in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege can be a vassal owing feudal service, so a subject of a lord.

clue.text: Old river redirected after introduction of new weather system

indicators.note: the new letter is introduced into the rearrangement
the river's course is changed, so the letters move

parts.note: the Nile is Africa's great river

explanation.surface: An old river changes course once a new climate pattern arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' turns O and NILE into ELINO; N is slipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño is the periodic warming of the Pacific that disrupts global climate.

clue.text: Predator that hurts head of lamb

parts.note: ow is the cry when something hurts

indicators.note: only the first letter of lamb

explanation.surface: A hunter injures the head of a lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A night bird of prey that hunts mice and voles.

clue.text: Tossing in the raw, without good pyjamas?

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, the jumble surrounds the good letter
tossed about, the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tossing and turning naked in bed, minus their pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing' rearranges IN THE RAW and 'without' wraps it round G.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas are an example of clothes for bed, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Good to take first place in race, prompting excess enthusiasm

indicators.note: the good letter replaces the opening letter of the race word

parts.note: to rush is to race

explanation.surface: Winning a race prompts an outpouring of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take first place in' puts G in place of the R of RUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush is to talk with effusive, over-the-top enthusiasm.

clue.text: Poetic vision possibly supported by cinema chain

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, which may set out a vision
resting on something means it supports you, giving on

explanation.surface: A poet's vision is backed by a chain of cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a British chain of picture houses.

clue.text: Record shortening applied to a remarkable racecourse

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the word is clipped by its final letter

parts.note: some can mean a remarkable, as in 'that was some race'

explanation.surface: A clipped record time at a superb racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortening' removes the last E of SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey stages the Derby, England's most famous flat horse race.

clue.text: Troubled land once invaded by King shown by English historian

indicators.note: the king's letter enters the jumble
disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is for rex, king

explanation.surface: A historian describes a troubled land once overrun by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' rearranges LAND ONCE and 'invaded by' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Hyde, Earl of Clarendon, wrote the History of the Rebellion on the English Civil War.
